correctness.rationale: For a full-row-rank gradient G=AO, the first updated gradient is BO with OO^T=I and B=A−(tr A/tr H)H symmetric and traceless. Its two eigenvalues are opposite, so its Gram matrix after multiplication by O is a scalar identity, including the zero case. On the nonzero equal-singular-value manifold the nuclear-scaled polar direction is 2G. The multiplier C=I−2H/tr H preserves that manifold because C^2=ρ^2 I; it commutes with H, giving the stated error and objective identities. G1=0 iff A=(tr A/tr H)H, equivalently the initial error is a positive multiple of a row isometry on the full-rank stratum. At rank one the canonical polar direction scales to G, and the invertible multiplier I−H/tr H gives the claimed slower factor along the low-curvature eigenspace. Nonterminating rank-two starts approach that rank-one start because the nonzero equal-singular-value termination set cannot accumulate there.
residual_risks: At rank one the thin SVD must mean the compact positive-singular-value decomposition; this is fixed by the explicitly specified canonical partial isometry.

The packaged rational checker propagates the proposed tail multiplier rather than independently recomputing the nonlinear update; the universal claim is established by the algebra, not the finite checks.

value.rationale: The result replaces an asymptotic bound for a nonlinear optimizer by an exact identification time and complete linear tail for arbitrary full-rank two-row starts, including noncommuting polar and curvature factors.
